ashby:jane:2d2a4d4b-25d1-4eb8-8c3b-6cd65.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Hey, I'm Liam https://www.linkedin.com/in/liamdmcdonald/, Group PM for Communications at Jane. I'm a New Zealander who's called Vancouver home for over 8 years, and outside of work you'll find me doing all the classic Pacific Northwest things: 50+ ski days a year, with the rest filled by hiking, biking and beaches (a sign of my Kiwi roots). I've spent most of my career building communications products in healthcare, and the rest in marketing automation. I came to Jane for the chance to shape the future of Jane and healthcare communication, and nine months in, both the opportunity and my excitement have only grown.

This role exists because our ambitions for Communications are growing. Much of a clinic's patient communication still happens outside of Jane, and it's one of the biggest demands on their time. You'll focus on net new areas, like additional channels, that bring more of that communication into Jane, and on where AI can help clinics stay on top of it. Alongside both, you'll contribute to some of our existing domains, like our Notifications Centre.

Our group is full of zero-to-one builders who are helping to shape the future of Jane and of healthcare, and you'll play a key role in that. You'll own a problem space end-to-end and take new products from idea to launch, but you won't be doing it alone - we've built a culture of collaboration where everyone, engineers included, helps shape the outcomes we focus on and the work that gets us there. If that sounds like your cup of tea, and you like to work hard, be kind, and have fun while you're at it, you'll be in great company - and I'd love to meet you.




WHAT IMPACT WE’RE LOOKING FOR YOU TO MAKE

 - Own a problem space within Communication from discovery and customer research through to shipping and GTM commercialization. You'll bring clarity to new, ambiguous areas and use good judgement to make decisions, knowing when there's enough information to move forward and when it's worth digging deeper.

 - Collaborate closely with partners beyond the PM, designer and engineer trio, including support, product marketing and communications design. At Jane, these partners play a core role in shaping our product, so you'll bring them in early and work with them throughout.

 - Work in the details, side by side with your engineers and designer, because this isn't a strategy-only role. Much of our work is zero to one, so you'll get tactical: refining edge cases, working through trade-offs, testing early prototypes and iterating until the solution is right.

 - Shape how we leverage AI in Communications in support of our group's mission and Jane's. You'll partner with the teams driving Jane's broader AI strategy, building on what they're creating and helping influence where it goes next, because it's not something any one group can do alone.

 - Partner with the design and engineering leads on your team to define the customer problems you're solving and the expected outcomes. Together, you'll build a roadmap around them and make the calls on what to prioritize, what to try first and what to say no to, bringing others along with you as you go.

 - Consistently solve problems that matter to our users, working backwards from each one to a right-sized solution that makes a difference for our customers and for Jane. You'll know our customers and the competitive landscape so well that you become the go-to expert in your space




WHAT EXPERIENCE WE NEED

 - 5+ years of product management experience in a SaaS company, including taking a product from 0-to-1. You've spotted an opportunity, won buy-in for it and shaped the plan to bring it to market, from deciding how to validate early ideas through to wider testing like betas, and built the confidence needed to commercialize it.

 - Experience leading planning and strategy work, from shaping a longer-term vision for your space to breaking it into clear priorities. You're a confident facilitator who is comfortable running workshops to explore problems, shape ideas and reach decisions.

 - A track record of shipping products that made a clear difference for customers, rather than a company-wide revenue number you contributed a slice of. You're comfortable defining what success looks like and using data to guide your decisions along the way.

 - Experience shipping AI-powered products and features that solve customer problems, and across the wider company, where you've helped influence a broader AI strategy by building alongside other teams rather than going it alone.

 - You've worked with a broad group of partners and built alignment in a fast-moving environment without slowing things down. You're skilled at communicating complex problems and solutions clearly and bringing senior leaders and other stakeholders into your thinking, which is core to how Jane works. For example, every week, there's a forum where anyone can share their work and get feedback from company leadership

 - If you've worked in communications, healthcare, AI or adjacent spaces like marketing automation, built SMB or B2C products, or navigated a regulated environment, that's a plus, but not required to apply.

"If you don't meet every single qualification but are excited about this role, we'd still love to hear from you."




MORE ABOUT JANE

Jane is a founder-led, high-growth SaaS company with a remote-first team working across Canada, the US, and the UK, united by our mission to help the helpers.

We build the products and tools that thousands of clinics rely on every day to run their businesses, care for their patients, and grow their communities. That level of impact means every person at Jane plays an important role in how we show up for our customers. We're all responsible for being deeply connected to their needs, obsessed with improving their experience, and proud of the difference our work makes in their day-to-day lives.

Jane is growing fast, and that growth brings exciting challenges that call for adaptability, resilience, learning agility, and humility. We're proud of what we've built and quick to admit what we don't know yet. We listen, learn, and adjust as we go. More than 70,000 businesses run on Jane which has 250,000+ practitioners interacting with our product on a daily basis and growth is continuing to accelerate.

Our goal isn't just delivery - it's delight. We move quickly, communicate openly, and solve real problems together. If you're energized by ambiguity, motivated by impact, and eager to learn with others, you'll thrive at Jane.




COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

At Jane, we're committed to paying fairly, clearly, and above all, paying for growth. This role has an annual salary range of CAD $117,100 to CAD $182,900. While that is a large range, it is intentional. It reflects the full growth journey someone might take in the role, from developing skills early on to becoming highly proficient and ultimately achieving excellence.

Most new hires join at the accomplished stage, which for this role represents an annual salary of CAD $139,000. A starting salary below this typically indicates a candidate with strong potential who is still developing key skills. Salaries above this usually apply to existing team members who have made a significant impact and bring deep Jane-specific knowledge.

We believe in paying for growth. You’ll have regular career development conversations with your manager and your compensation will grow as you gain experience and contribute meaningfully to our mission.

Paying clearly is one of our compensation fundamentals. Watch this https://vimeo.com/880258361 short video to learn how our salary bands are set. You’re also encouraged to ask questions about compensation at any point during the interview process.

We also offer a comprehensive benefits package, You can learn more about it here https://jane.app/documents/hiring/jane_benefits_overview.pdf!


Jane takes job scams and candidate fraud seriously. Jane will only contact you from an @jane.app http://jane.app email address. We'll never contact you from a personal email, ask for payment, or request purchases during the hiring process. If something doesn't seem right, please reach out to us at hiring@jane.app before sharing any personal information.

AT KLUE https://klue.com/, WE’RE BUILDING THE FUTURE OF COMPETITIVE INTELLIGENCE




👋 KLUE PRODUCT IS HIRING!

You're the PM who wants the whole thing: the strategy, the roadmap, the pricing conversation, the launch, and the number at the end of it. You're comfortable making the call before you have every answer, and you use AI tools every day because that's how you build now.



You'll report to the VP Product and work alongside a dedicated engineering and design team who are building this product with you. You'll work with Marketing and Sales on how it goes to market, and you'll spend real time with the customers using it. When someone asks where this product is going and why, you're the one with the answer.



Your Mission? To double Klue’s revenue in 12 months by building something customers keep coming back for, Sales can sell on their own, and the market hears about. You own the strategy, the quality bar and the commercial outcome. When the product wins, you win.




WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU

You'll learn what it takes to build an AI-first product from the ground up: how it's shaped, priced, sold and made good. That's a different craft from bolting AI onto something that already exists, and very few companies are doing it at this stage. The scope is clear and the target is big, so a year from now you'll know exactly what you built and what it moved.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the strategy and roadmap. You decide where the Product goes, what gets built, what gets cut and in what order. You'll make the case to our VP, Product and exec team, weigh near-term revenue against longer bets, and stand behind the calls you make. You'll also set the shipping rhythm with the engineering and design team so customers notice the product getting better over time.

 - Run your own discovery. Sit in on customer calls and talk to users directly. Build a repeatable loop that turns feedback into prioritized decisions, bring evidence into roadmap debates, and know the customer base well enough to spot which segment the next bet is for.

 - Set the quality bar for AI. Work with engineering on model quality and evals: what good output looks like and how we measure it. Stay close enough to what's technically possible that you can reshape the roadmap when it shifts. Enterprise customers need to trust an AI product before they rely on it, and you'll define what earns that trust.

 - Collaborate with Sales & Marketing. Guide marketing with positioning. Enable Sales so reps can run the conversation on their own. Partner with Demand Gen on the pipeline this product needs to generate, and bring whatever is blocking deals back into the roadmap.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

We want you to love the role you're in and believe these skills and experiences will help you be successful! You'll know you're nailing it when:

 - Revenue Growth. Product revenue doubles within 12 months.

 - Shipped Changes. A much better version is live within 2 weeks, usage is up, and customers are asking for more without being chased.

 - Retention improves year over year.  Retention on this product improves year over year, and every churn has a known reason that's traceable to a product decision or a deliberate trade-off.

 - The product builds its own pipeline. The product is generating its own pipeline and Sales can run the pitch without pulling you in.

 - Customer Feedback. A running discovery cadence you own, with a clear line from what customers said to what got built.

 - Product Quality. Evals and a defined quality bar are in place for the AI surface, and output quality is trending up against them.

 - Independent Ownership. You run this product without the VP, Product in the detail. Hard calls still get escalated, you just arrive with a recommendation and the thinking behind it, so the conversation starts from your point of view.




WHAT YOU BRING

Must-Haves

 - 0 to 1 experience. You've taken a product or major product line from nothing to real revenue, and you can walk us through what you got wrong along the way.

 - AI-native. You build with AI tools daily and have a clear view of what models can and can't do today.

 - GTM thinking. You've owned or been accountable for a number, and you treat pricing, packaging and go-to-market as part of the product job.

 - Consumer-grade UX for enterprise buyers. You've built products where the user and the buyer are different people, and you've met a high bar for both.

 - Decisive with incomplete information. You make the call, move, and change course fast when the evidence says to.

 - Hands-on discovery. You talk to customers directly and regularly, and you trust that over a summary.

Nice-to-Haves

 - Experience with a competitive intelligence, market intelligence or research product, or selling into that buyer.

 - Technical enough to dig into evals and model behaviour with engineers yourself.

At Klue, we're committed to building a high-performing team where people feel a strong sense of belonging, can be their authentic selves, and are able to reach their full potential. If there’s anything we can do to make our hiring process more accessible or to better support you, please let us know, we’re happy to accommodate.







WHY KLUE MIGHT BE THE PERFECT FIT FOR YOU

At Klue, you’ll push the boundaries of what’s possible. For yourself, your team, and our customers. The environment here feels more startup than corporate. You’ll roll up your sleeves, build, iterate, and level up. This is a place where your ideas matter, you can shape what comes next, and leave your mark.

If you’re looking to join a category-defining company… where you own big outcomes, influence real customers, and work with smart, gritty people… you’ll thrive here.                         



Unlock Your Potential. Take Risks. Take Action. Innovate




HOW WE WORK AT KLUE

We love the balance of connection and flexibility. We work Office-First, with a hybrid touch, and work together in our vibrant offices on Mondays, Wednesdays & Thursdays to collaborate, brainstorm, and build together.

ABOUT KOHO

We’re on a mission to make financial services better for every Canadian. That means no hidden fees, no predatory interest rates - just financial products designed to help our users spend smart, save more, and build real wealth. We’re a performance organization with a strong heart: we care deeply about outcomes, and everything ties back to our mission - to financially empower a generation of Canadians.

At KOHO, we’re not your average 9-5. We believe real impact comes from people who are trusted, empowered, and supported to do their best work - without sacrificing their lives to do it. We prioritize work-life integration, not just work-life balance. That means asynchronous collaboration, flexible hours, and a remote-first setup built around autonomy and high trust.

KOHO is entering its next chapter - leaner, smarter, more AI-integrated. We’re building for impact, not bureaucracy. If you thrive in environments that value clarity, ownership, and bold thinking, you’ll fit right in.



About The Role

We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager to join KOHO’s Growth team. You’ll lead a dedicated growth pod focused on one of our highest-leverage problems: either converting more registered users into active customers, or building product-led channels that acquire users through the product itself.



This is a metrics-driven role with clear ownership and real P&L impact. You’ll run experiments at high velocity, own a specific set of growth KPIs, and work within a cross-functional pod (engineering, design, data) to move them. You won’t be maintaining a feature backlog — you’ll be solving growth problems end-to-end.



What You’ll Be Doing

 - Own growth metrics with clear accountability. You’ll be responsible for specific KPIs tied to user acquisition or activation — metrics that directly impact KOHO’s revenue and unit economics.

 - Run experiments at high velocity. Design, ship, and iterate on growth initiatives weekly. Maintain a rolling experiment backlog with clear hypotheses and success criteria. Learn fast from failures.

 - Build business cases grounded in data. Use quantitative analysis, financial modeling, and CAC/LTV economics to prioritize bets and defend investment decisions to leadership.

 - Lead a cross-functional pod. Work with engineering, design, data, and marketing to ship growth initiatives. Align your team around a single mission and keep execution tight.

 - Identify and reduce friction across the user journey. Whether it’s funnel drop-offs, onboarding bottlenecks, or underperforming growth channels — diagnose root causes and ship solutions.

 - Design and scale growth loops. Think beyond linear funnels. Identify opportunities for compounding, product-led mechanics that reduce acquisition costs over time.

 - Collaborate across the growth org. Work closely with the other growth pod to ensure the full user journey — from first touch to active customer — works as a connected system.

 - Communicate strategy to leadership. Present growth strategy, experiment results, and roadmap decisions to executive audiences through quarterly strategy reviews.



Who You Are

 - 3–5+ years of product management experience, with at least 2 years focused on growth, activation, acquisition, or product-led growth at a consumer or fintech company.

 - Track record of moving growth metrics — whether that’s conversion funnels, referral programs, onboarding flows, or acquisition loops. We want to see specific numbers you’ve moved.

 - Deeply data-driven. You can write SQL when needed, design experiments with statistical rigor, and make decisions based on CAC/LTV modeling rather than intuition.

 - High experiment velocity. You’re comfortable shipping multiple experiments per sprint, learning quickly from failures, and iterating without over-engineering.

 - Cross-functional leader. You’ve led pods or squads (engineering, design, marketing, data) and know how to align a team around a single metric.

 - Strong strategic communicator. You can articulate growth strategy to executives, write compelling business cases, and translate data into narratives that drive alignment.

 - AI-native. You actively use AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity, etc.) in your daily work — for analysis, writing, research, and prototyping.



Nice to Have

 - Experience at a Canadian fintech or a regulated financial services company.

 - Familiarity with product analytics, martech, and BI tools — our core product and growth stack.

 - Experience with A/B testing platforms (Eppo, Optimizely, or similar) and experiment governance.

 - Background in behavioural economics, incentive design, or conversion optimization.

 - Experience with fintech onboarding and KYC optimization — reducing friction in regulated sign-up flows.

 - Experience building product-led acquisition at scale.



The budgeted salary range for this role is $160,000 - $200,000 CAD / year.

At KOHO, we are dedicated to providing pay transparency to all candidates. Compensation at KOHO is determined through various factors including but not limited to: comparable salary market data within Canada, technical skill assessment, a holistic view of previous work history, and internal pay equity with other KOHO team members.




DESCRIPTION DE POSTE EN FRANÇAIS




À PROPOS DU POSTE

Nous sommes à la recherche d’un(e) gestionnaire de produits principal(e) pour se joindre à l’équipe Croissance de KOHO. Vous dirigerez une cellule de croissance dédiée à l’un de nos enjeux à plus fort effet de levier : soit convertir davantage d’utilisateurs inscrits en clients actifs, soit bâtir des canaux axés sur le produit qui permettent d’acquérir des utilisateurs par l’entremise du produit lui-même.

Il s’agit d’un poste axé sur les indicateurs, assorti de responsabilités claires et d’une incidence réelle sur les résultats financiers. Vous mènerez des expérimentations à un rythme soutenu, serez responsable d’un ensemble précis d’indicateurs clés de croissance et travaillerez au sein d’une cellule interfonctionnelle (ingénierie, design, données) pour les faire progresser. Vous ne gérerez pas un carnet de fonctionnalités : vous résoudrez des problèmes de croissance de bout en bout.




CE QUE VOUS FEREZ

 - Prendre en charge des indicateurs de croissance avec une responsabilité claire. Vous serez responsable d’indicateurs clés de performance précis liés à l’acquisition ou à l’activation des utilisateurs, des indicateurs qui ont une incidence directe sur les revenus et l’économie unitaire de KOHO.

 - Mener des expérimentations à un rythme soutenu. Concevoir, lancer et itérer des initiatives de croissance chaque semaine. Tenir à jour un carnet d’expérimentations continu, assorti d’hypothèses et de critères de réussite clairs. Tirer rapidement des leçons des échecs.

 - Élaborer des analyses de rentabilité fondées sur les données. Utiliser l’analyse quantitative, la modélisation financière et l’économie CAC/VVC (coût d’acquisition client et valeur vie client) pour prioriser les paris et défendre les décisions d’investissement auprès de la direction.

 - Diriger une cellule interfonctionnelle. Travailler avec les équipes d’ingénierie, de design, de données et de marketing pour lancer des initiatives de croissance. Rallier votre équipe autour d’une mission unique et assurer une exécution rigoureuse.

 - Cerner et réduire les points de friction tout au long du parcours utilisateur. Qu’il s’agisse d’abandons dans l’entonnoir, de goulots d’étranglement à l’intégration ou de canaux de croissance peu performants, diagnostiquer les causes profondes et mettre en œuvre des solutions.

 - Concevoir et déployer à grande échelle des boucles de croissance. Penser au-delà des entonnoirs linéaires. Repérer les occasions de mécanismes cumulatifs axés sur le produit qui réduisent les coûts d’acquisition au fil du temps.

 - Collaborer avec l’ensemble de l’organisation Croissance. Travailler en étroite collaboration avec l’autre cellule de croissance afin que l’ensemble du parcours utilisateur, du premier contact jusqu’au client actif, fonctionne comme un système intégré.

 - Communiquer la stratégie à la direction. Présenter la stratégie de croissance, les résultats des expérimentations et les décisions relatives à la feuille de route aux membres de la haute direction dans le cadre de revues stratégiques trimestrielles.




VOTRE PROFIL

 - De 3 à 5 ans ou plus d’expérience en gestion de produits, dont au moins 2 ans axés sur la croissance, l’activation, l’acquisition ou la croissance axée sur le produit au sein d’une entreprise grand public ou de technologie financière (fintech).

 - Feuille de route démontrée en matière d’amélioration des indicateurs de croissance, qu’il s’agisse d’entonnoirs de conversion, de programmes de recommandation, de parcours d’intégration ou de boucles d’acquisition. Nous voulons connaître les chiffres précis que vous avez fait progresser.

 - Approche résolument axée sur les données. Vous savez écrire des requêtes SQL au besoin, concevoir des expérimentations avec rigueur statistique et prendre des décisions fondées sur la modélisation CAC/VVC plutôt que sur l’intuition.

 - Rythme d’expérimentation élevé. Vous êtes à l’aise de lancer plusieurs expérimentations par sprint, de tirer rapidement des leçons des échecs et d’itérer sans complexifier inutilement.

 - Leader interfonctionnel(le). Vous avez dirigé des cellules ou des équipes (ingénierie, design, marketing, données) et savez rallier une équipe autour d’un indicateur unique.

 - Communicateur(trice) stratégique hors pair. Vous savez exposer une stratégie de croissance à la haute direction, rédiger des analyses de rentabilité convaincantes et traduire les données en récits qui favorisent l’adhésion.

 - Adepte de l’IA. Vous utilisez activement des outils d’IA (Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity, etc.) dans votre travail quotidien, que ce soit pour l’analyse, la rédaction, la recherche ou le prototypage.




ATOUTS

 - Expérience au sein d’une entreprise canadienne de technologie financière ou d’une société de services financiers réglementée.

 - Connaissance des outils d’analyse de produits, de technologie marketing (martech) et d’informatique décisionnelle (BI), qui forment le cœur de notre pile technologique produit et croissance.

 - Expérience des plateformes de tests A/B (Eppo, Optimizely ou autres) et de la gouvernance des expérimentations.

 - Formation en économie comportementale, en conception de mesures incitatives ou en optimisation de la conversion.

 - Expérience de l’intégration des clients en technologie financière et de l’optimisation des processus de vérification d’identité (KYC), afin de réduire la friction dans les parcours d’inscription réglementés.

 - Expérience dans la mise en place d’une acquisition axée sur le produit à grande échelle.
   
   


RÉMUNÉRATION

L’échelle salariale prévue pour ce poste se situe entre 160 000 $ et 200 000 $ CA par année.

Chez KOHO, nous nous engageons à offrir une transparence salariale à tous les candidats. La rémunération est déterminée en fonction de plusieurs facteurs, notamment les données comparatives du marché canadien, l’évaluation des compétences techniques, l’expérience professionnelle globale du candidat ainsi que l’équité salariale interne au sein de l’équipe KOHO.

Hi there! Thanks for stopping by 👋

We're looking for a Staff Technical Program Manager to join our Product & Technology Operations team and own how we build the Product Development Lifecycle (PDLC) into a shared execution model across Product, Engineering, and Design.

You will own how work flows from idea to impact across the organization - one language for how work moves, one set of metrics leaders can trust, and one standard for what "good" looks like at every stage of PDLC.

This is a founding role for the function. You'll define the model, align stakeholders around it, and prove out its value as you build.




What you’ll be doing:

Define the execution model

 - Design a PDLC framework that works across Product, Engineering, and Design and across all Lightspeed products.

 - Define what good looks like at each stage of PDLC, including the artifacts, checkpoints, and exit criteria teams should use.

Build the measurement system

 - Establish metrics that give leaders a trustworthy, holistic view of how work is flowing and where it's getting stuck.

 - Design the framework so it measures the system and surfaces bottlenecks, not individual performance.

 - Build in exception tracking so blocked or off-track work is visible early.

Drive adoption

 - Partner with Product, Engineering, and Design leaders across every vertical to align on the model and earn genuine buy-in and adoption.

 - Navigate real differences across verticals and business units without forcing false consistency where it doesn't make sense.

 - Bring structure to ambiguity - resolve open questions as they surface rather than waiting for a perfect spec.

Build an AI-first PDLC

 - Define what humans own versus what AI agents own at each stage of PDLC, keeping judgment, accountability, and anything irreversible or customer-facing with humans.

 - Partner with Engineering to identify where AI agents can accelerate delivery, build pilots, and measure their ROI and impact on speed.

 - Ensure human checkpoints are genuine decisions, not rubber stamps, as adoption scales.

Evolve the model

 - Treat the framework as a living system - review it periodically and adjust based on what's actually working.

 - Report on program health and progress to senior leadership.



What you need to bring:

 - Experience designing or significantly evolving a delivery framework, execution model, or program management system - not just operating one someone else built.

 - Experience leading cross-functional organizations through operational change, including turning skepticism into genuine adoption.

 - A track record of building measurement systems from ambiguous or inconsistent data, and knowing which problems to solve first versus defer.

 - Experience partnering with Engineering on applied AI or automation, including how to evaluate and measure whether it's actually accelerating delivery, not just novel.

 - Strong executive communication skills - able to represent program health, risk, and trade-offs credibly to senior leadership.

 - Demonstrated ability to influence and align senior stakeholders across Product, Engineering, and Design without formal authority over them.

 - Comfort operating with significant ambiguity and independently structuring a path forward rather than waiting for direction.

 - As a global company with employees and clients outside of Quebec, fluency in English as a working language is required for this position


YOU'D BE GREAT AT THIS ROLE IF YOU...

 - Enjoy building something from a blank page rather than optimizing an existing system.

 - Can hold a strong point of view on "what good looks like" while staying open to what the data and teams tell you.

 - Get energized aligning stakeholders with different views, perspectives, and backgrounds.

 - Think in systems and flow, not individual tickets or teams.
   
   

We know that people are more than what’s on their CV. If you’re unsure that you have the right profile for the role... hit the ‘Apply’ button and give it a try!



Be a changemaker

You’ll enjoy:

 - A flexible work environment that empowers you to do your best work

 - A culture that celebrates performance

 - The chance to make an impact in a team that’s big enough for career growth, but lean enough to make your voice heard

 - Career-defining opportunities

Plus benefits designed to keep you happy, healthy and fulfilled.

 - Flexible paid time off and remote work policies

 - Equity options, because this is your company too

 - Contributions to your pension plan. Your future matters

 - Training opportunities to grow your skills and career

 - Health and wellness credit so you feel your best

 - Time off to volunteer and give back to your community

 - Interest groups, employee led networks, social committees to sponsored sports teams

 - Computer purchase program to get your personal Macbook

 - Enhanced parental leave to support growing families
   
   

Fuel your growth. Find your people.

At Lightspeed, your growth is our priority. We invest in you with continuous learning opportunities, global mobility and benefits designed to support you—all within a driven, diverse and inclusive team that’s passionate about empowering our communities.



 Please note that we ask applicants to disclose any criminal convictions, and we conduct criminal record checks as part of our hiring process for this role.

Lightspeed is a proud equal opportunity employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive and barrier-free workplace. Lightspeed welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.




WHERE TO FROM HERE?

Obviously, this has to be mutually beneficial: we want you to step into a role you love, and we want to offer you a place you’re proud to come to every day. For a glimpse into our world check out our career page here https://www.lightspeedhq.com/careers/.

Lightspeed is building communities through commerce, and we need people from all backgrounds and lived experiences to do that. We were founded in 2005, in Montreal’s gay village and our original members were all part of the LGBTQ+ community. The ethos of our business has been about inclusion from the very beginning, and we strive to provide a workplace where everyone belongs.

Powering the businesses that are the backbone of the global economy, Lightspeed's one-stop commerce platform helps merchants innovate to simplify, scale, and provide exceptional customer experiences. Our cloud commerce solution transforms and unifies online and physical operations, multichannel sales, expansion to new locations, global payments, financial solutions, and connection to supplier networks.

Founded in Montréal, Canada in 2005, Lightspeed is dual-listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: LSPD) and Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: LSPD). With teams across North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, the company serves retail, hospitality, and golf businesses in over 100 countries.

Hi there! Thanks for stopping by 👋

We're looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager to join our Product & Technology Operations team and own how we manage, optimize, and scale cloud, vendor, and AI spend across the organization.

You will define the FinOps strategy itself - not just run an existing cost program, but decide what gets optimized, in what order, and why. Cloud and vendor cost management has an established playbook that we want to scale and automate; AI spend does not. You'll be defining and building FinOps for AI, while also evolving existing practice into a more automated system.

This is a very senior technical IC role. You'll bring enough technical depth to build or directly shape the automations, dashboards, and optimization recommendations yourself, and enough strategic judgment to influence how leadership thinks about cost trade-offs and how we partner with Finance, Procurement and other functions on all things vendor management and optimizations.



What you’ll be doing:

Define the FinOps strategy

 - Own the strategy for cloud, vendor, and AI cost management across the organization - not just the execution of an existing roadmap.

 - Continuously reassess what to optimize, in what order, and why, based on where spend and risk are actually concentrated.

 - Build the framework for managing AI cost, an area with no established industry playbook yet.

Drive cost optimization with technical depth

 - Analyze cloud usage, vendor contracts, and AI spend to identify inefficiencies and develop strategies to reduce unnecessary cost.

 - Build or directly shape the dashboards, automations, and monitoring systems that make cost visible and actionable, at a technical depth equivalent to a Senior Engineer.

 - Propose specific technical optimizations, not just process recommendations, and know when a suggestion requires deeper engineering partnership.

 - Apply hands-on experience building and automating with AI, not just directing others to do it.

Lead the program across the organization

 - Oversee and in some cases execute multiple cost-optimization initiatives simultaneously.

 - Own the reporting structure - cost attribution, monitoring, and alerting - and use it to tell leadership a clear, trustworthy story about spend and savings.

 - Partner with FP&A to define and establish key cost metrics giving leadership a sharper financial lens on cost efficiency.

 - Manage cross-functional dependencies, risk, and change across SRE, Engineering, Data, FP&A, and Procurement teams.

Influence at the executive level

 - Bring insights on feasibility, timelines, risk, and cost trade-offs directly to senior and executive stakeholders, shaping decisions that affect real budget and infrastructure choices.

 - Balance centralized cost management standards with the autonomy individual business units need to operate effectively.

 - Proactively surface issues and advocate for change across products and teams, rather than waiting to be asked.

Mentorship

 - Partner with Delivery Ops leadership on TPM career development, best practices, and the foundation of the broader TPM function.

 - Mentor other TPMs, helping raise the technical and strategic bar across the team.



What you need to bring:

 - Experience owning both the strategy and execution for a cloud, vendor or AI cost optimization program - not just executing one someone else designed.

 - Deep knowledge of the AI vendor landscape - pricing models, contract structures, and the specific optimization levers and nuances that differ from traditional cloud cost management.

 - Technical depth in cloud architecture, cost management, and optimization techniques strong enough to build or directly evaluate dashboards and automation yourself.

 - Experience navigating an area with no established playbook, building the framework as you go rather than applying a known model.

 - A track record of running large, cross-organizational programs spanning multiple business units.

 - Strong executive communication skills - able to translate complex technical and cost trade-offs into decisions leadership can act on.

 - Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and drive change across an organization without formal authority over them.

Hi there! Thanks for stopping by 👋

We're looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager to join our Product & Technology Operations team and own how we manage, optimize, and scale cloud, vendor, and AI spend across the organization.

You will define the FinOps strategy itself - not just run an existing cost program, but decide what gets optimized, in what order, and why. Cloud and vendor cost management has an established playbook that we want to scale and automate; AI spend does not. You'll be defining and building FinOps for AI, while also evolving existing practice into a more automated system.

This is a very senior technical IC role. You'll bring enough technical depth to build or directly shape the automations, dashboards, and optimization recommendations yourself, and enough strategic judgment to influence how leadership thinks about cost trade-offs and how we partner with Finance, Procurement and other functions on all things vendor management and optimizations.

 

What you’ll be doing:

Define the FinOps strategy

 - Own the strategy for cloud, vendor, and AI cost management across the organization - not just the execution of an existing roadmap.

 - Continuously reassess what to optimize, in what order, and why, based on where spend and risk are actually concentrated.

 - Build the framework for managing AI cost, an area with no established industry playbook yet.

Drive cost optimization with technical depth

 - Analyze cloud usage, vendor contracts, and AI spend to identify inefficiencies and develop strategies to reduce unnecessary cost.

 - Build or directly shape the dashboards, automations, and monitoring systems that make cost visible and actionable, at a technical depth equivalent to a Senior Engineer.

 - Propose specific technical optimizations, not just process recommendations, and know when a suggestion requires deeper engineering partnership.

 - Apply hands-on experience building and automating with AI, not just directing others to do it.

Lead the program across the organization

 - Oversee and in some cases execute multiple cost-optimization initiatives simultaneously.

 - Own the reporting structure - cost attribution, monitoring, and alerting - and use it to tell leadership a clear, trustworthy story about spend and savings.

 - Partner with FP&A to define and establish key cost metrics giving leadership a sharper financial lens on cost efficiency.

 - Manage cross-functional dependencies, risk, and change across SRE, Engineering, Data, FP&A, and Procurement teams.

Influence at the executive level

 - Bring insights on feasibility, timelines, risk, and cost trade-offs directly to senior and executive stakeholders, shaping decisions that affect real budget and infrastructure choices.

 - Balance centralized cost management standards with the autonomy individual business units need to operate effectively.

 - Proactively surface issues and advocate for change across products and teams, rather than waiting to be asked.

Mentorship

 - Partner with Delivery Ops leadership on TPM career development, best practices, and the foundation of the broader TPM function.

 - Mentor other TPMs, helping raise the technical and strategic bar across the team.

 

What you need to bring:

 - Experience owning both the strategy and execution for a cloud, vendor or AI cost optimization program - not just executing one someone else designed.

 - Deep knowledge of the AI vendor landscape - pricing models, contract structures, and the specific optimization levers and nuances that differ from traditional cloud cost management.

 - Technical depth in cloud architecture, cost management, and optimization techniques strong enough to build or directly evaluate dashboards and automation yourself.

 - Experience navigating an area with no established playbook, building the framework as you go rather than applying a known model.

 - A track record of running large, cross-organizational programs spanning multiple business units.

 - Strong executive communication skills - able to translate complex technical and cost trade-offs into decisions leadership can act on.

 - Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and drive change across an organization without formal authority over them.

We know that people are more than what’s on their CV. If you’re unsure that you have the right profile for the role... hit the ‘Apply’ button and give it a try!



Be a changemaker

You’ll enjoy:

 - A flexible work environment that empowers you to do your best work

 - A culture that celebrates performance

 - The chance to make an impact in a team that’s big enough for career growth, but lean enough to make your voice heard

 - Career-defining opportunities

Plus benefits designed to keep you happy, healthy and fulfilled.

 - Flexible paid time off and remote work policies

 - Equity options, because this is your company too

 - Contributions to your pension plan. Your future matters

 - Training opportunities to grow your skills and career

 - Health and wellness credit so you feel your best

 - Time off to volunteer and give back to your community

 - Interest groups, employee led networks, social committees to sponsored sports teams

 - Computer purchase program to get your personal Macbook

 - Enhanced parental leave to support growing families

Fuel your growth. Find your people.

At Lightspeed, your growth is our priority. We invest in you with continuous learning opportunities, global mobility and benefits designed to support you—all within a driven, diverse and inclusive team that’s passionate about empowering our communities

ashby:loopio:906f8e02-053b-424d-a163-261.description:
TAKE YOUR CAREER TO NEW HEIGHTS WITH LOOPIO! 🚀✨



We're looking for a Staff Product Manager for a strategically important initiative: building a headless experience for Loopio’s platform, making it openly accessible and interoperable across the broader enterprise AI ecosystem through other AI assistants, agent frameworks rather than locking it inside Loopio's own interface.

This role is built for an AI builder who deeply understands the future of agentic workflows in enterprise organizations. You are comfortable operating with significant autonomy, with end-to-end ownership of critical initiatives.. You'll take initiatives from early concept through product-market fit and into scaled adoption, working alongside our established, high-usage product.

The ideal candidate has direct experience shipping successful agentic B2B SaaS experiences, a track record of launching and driving success with product, data, and workflow integrations across a wide range of B2B products, along with a metrics-driven approach to proving what works before scaling.

 

 Note: This is an existing vacancy on the team 

 
 


💻 WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

 - Product Vision & Strategy
   
   - Define and own the product vision for your ownership scope.
   
   - Translate company objectives, overall product vision, and market opportunity into a roadmap that sequences from early validation to scaled adoption.
   
   - Set clear success metrics for each phase of the initiative and hold the team accountable to them.
   
   - Create internal and external alignment and excitement for the interoperable future you will be creating.

 - Building & Execution
   
   - Collaborate closely with your partners in design and engineering to create a strongly aligned and focused team.
   
   - Drive discovery to validate problem, solution, and willingness-to-pay before over-investing in build.
   
   - Ship early, learn fast, and iterate based on real usage rather than assumption.
   
   - Navigate the specific challenge of exposing Loopio's knowledge outside its own interface: balancing openness and interoperability against data security, partner trust, and platform control.
   
   - Drive adoption post-launch: this role doesn't stop at shipping a v1, you fully own the realization of the customer and business outcomes we set out to achieve.

 - Integration & Platform Design
   
   - Develop a strong point of view on what makes an MCP Server, API, connector, or integration genuinely great for developers and partners, not just technically functional, and translate that into product decisions.
   
   - Partner closely with engineering on API design, MCP server, tool, and skills architecture, connectors, auth, and data contracts, enough to make informed product calls without needing to be talked through the fundamentals.
   
   - Design for interoperability and trust: how Loopio's knowledge is exposed to other AI assistants and agent frameworks without compromising security or control.

 - Customer & Market Focus
   
   - Deeply understand the workflows of enterprise customers and technical stakeholders who need Loopio's knowledge available inside their own systems and agent ecosystems.
   
   - Run discovery directly with customers and prospects to validate problems and success criteria.
   
   - Track the competitive and market landscape for headless, API-first, and agent-interoperable platforms.

 - Autonomy & Influence
   
   - Operate independently, spotting gaps and opportunities without needing direction, and rallying the right people to move on them.
   
   - Communicate vision, progress, and metrics clearly to executives, cross-functional stakeholders, and customers.
   
   - Act as an internal thought leader on what great integration and interoperability experiences look like.

 


✨ WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO THE TEAM

 - Track record of designing and launching MCP servers, APIs, and other integrations that connect systems together, ideally with direct experience shipping enterprise integrations or connectors in a B2B SaaS context.

 - We care more about this track record than a specific years-of-experience threshold; strong candidates may come from a range of tenure levels.

 - Experience taking a brand-new product from zero to launch and adoption, or experience in enterprise workflows, sales tech, security questionnaires, or proposal/RFP automation, is a plus, not a requirement.

 - Startup, founder, or prior engineering/technical background is a plus.

 - Working knowledge of API design, MCP server architecture, auth, data contracts, and versioning, and the trade-offs involved (developer experience, security, backward compatibility).

 - Working knowledge of LLMs and agent frameworks, enough to understand how Loopio's knowledge would be consumed by other AI assistants and agents.

 - Comfortable enough in the technical details to be a credible thought partner to engineering, without needing to be the one writing the code.

 - You are already adept at using AI tools for research, artifact building, prototype building, spec building, etc., across all areas of the PM role.

 - You bring proven product taste - you deeply understand what matters to developers, partners, and enterprise customers, and how to marry the right capabilities with an appropriate, secure, and delightful experience.

 - You have strong instincts in product discovery, prioritization, and execution, especially in ambiguous, early-stage environments.

 - You are metrics-driven: you define what success looks like before you build, and you know how to measure it after.

 - You have excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, and you are able to bring people along on a new and sometimes unproven direction.

 - Self-directed. You don't wait for a roadmap to tell you what's next.

 - Entrepreneurial and comfortable with ambiguity; energized by building something that doesn't exist yet.

 - Results-oriented, with a bias toward shipping and learning over long planning cycles.

 
 


WHERE YOU’LL WORK 📍

 - Loopio is a remote-first workplace because we recognize the advantages of working flexibly. We are HQ’d in Canada, with established hub regions around the world from which we hire.

 - Our employees (or Loopers, as we call ourselves!) live and work in 🇨🇦 Canada (British Columbia and Ontario), 🇬🇧 London, and 🇮🇳 India (specifically in Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Bengaluru).

 - The majority of our team is based in ON and BC, which means these employees live and work remotely within a 300km radius of Toronto (within Ontario) and Vancouver (Within BC). 

 - We offer flexible co-working locations available to Loopers in ON and BC. Those based in ON have the option of working out of our convenient co-working space located in the heart of Downtown Toronto and a 12-minute walk from Union Station. BC Loopers have the option to work centrally in Vancouver. It is whatever works best for you!

 - You’ll collaborate with your teams virtually across the UK, India, and North America (we’re just a Zoom call and Slack message away!) with core sync hours and focus time for headsdown work 🙇🏾 during the workday

 - We encourage asynchronous collaboration to effectively work as a global #OneTeam!

 


WHY YOU’LL ♥️ WORKING AT LOOPIO

 - Your manager supports your development by providing ongoing feedback and regular 1-on-1s, we leverage Lattice https://lattice.com/e-lp/talent-products?utm_source=google&utm_medium=paid-search&utm_campaign=NOAM_Google_Search_Brand_Core_Tier_1__OCT-Conv-Test-HR&utm_adgroup=Brand_Core_Tier_1&attribution=lattice-mktg&_bt=645279480236&_bk=lattice&_bm=p&_bn=g&_bg=149106216630&cq_src=google_ads&cq_cmp=19577143427&cq_con=149106216630&cq_term=lattice&cq_med=&cq_plac=&cq_net=g&cq_plt=gp&qgad=645279480236&qgterm=lattice&gad_source=1&gclid=Cj0KCQiA-5a9BhCBARIsACwMkJ4OzbQBp30JTrxoLWSv3ht4C0NBeu9uyrTE7GCIu8D_lqBGuC3CG7kaAiWnEALw_wcB for our 1:1s and performance conversations  

 - You will have the opportunity to elevate 🪄 your craft and the opportunity to explore your creativity, with a dedicated professional mastery allowance for more learning support! We encourage experimentation and innovative thinking to drive business impact.

 - We offer a wide range of health and wellness benefits https://loopio.com/perks-benefits/ to support your physical and mental well-being, starting day 1️⃣ with Loopio.

 - We’ll set you up to work remotely with a MacBook laptop 🍏, a monthly phone and internet subsidy, and a work-from-home budget to help get your home office all set up.  

 - You’ll be joining a supportive culture that has thoughtfully built out opportunities for connections in a remote first environment.

 - Participate in 🎤 townhalls, AMA (Ask-Me-Anything), and company celebrations to celebrate the big wins and milestones as #oneteam!

 - Our four  Employee Resource Groups https://loopio.com/annual-deib-report/ offer opportunities for employees to learn and connect year-round. 

 - You’ll be a part of an award-winning workplace 🏆with an opportunity to make a big impact on the business.

 

Questioning your qualifications? Read this ‼️ Hi there, we recognize that all too often, potential candidates don’t apply for a position simply because they don’t hit every single criteria included in the job description—particularly members of underrepresented groups. 

Whether or not your experience ✅ checks off all the boxes on a job posting, we still encourage you to apply to ensure that your application receives a review from our team. We understand that a resume can only showcase so much during the applicant stage, so we've created prompts in the application for you to share more about yourself. If you've made a career transition (or a few!), you’re self taught in a new role, or you have skills/experience you’d like to highlight, we want to hear more about what you could bring to the table.



AI in Recruitment  👩🏻‍💻  At Loopio, we leverage  artificial intelligence (AI) technology to enhance our recruitment process. These tools assist with tasks such as resume screening, drafting preliminary job descriptions, generating initial interview questions, transcription and occasionally sourcing prospective candidates. However, AI is never used to make final hiring decisions; our use of AI  serves to support repetitive and administrative tasks in order to streamline our hiring and recruitment workflows. We are committed to the responsible use of AI in our hiring practices, prioritizing both  an improved candidate experience and operational efficiency. Our standardized hiring practices remain focused on reducing biases, with all key hiring decisions  solely made by our team. We continuously review and refine our hiring practices to align with  industry best practices and evolving legal guidelines



AI Usage in Interviews 🤖 The Loopio interview process is designed to help us better understand your professional experiences, as well as your unique perspective and approach to delivery and collaboration. To ensure a fair and accurate assessment, we expect candidates to refrain from using AI-generated content to produce responses to our interview questions during the live interview, as our goal is to evaluate your own knowledge and problem-solving abilities - not those of an AI assistant. If AI-generated responses are identified during the interview, Loopio reserves the right to disqualify candidates from the interview process.

For specific roles that include a take-home assignment, our AI Interviewee Policy allows the use of AI for initial support; however, the final submission must be a true reflection of your personal insights, skills and decision-making.



Loopio is an equal opportunity employer that is deeply committed to building equitable workplaces that are diverse and inclusive. We actively encourage candidates from all backgrounds and lifestyles to consider us as a future employer. Please contact a member of our Talent Experience team (work@loopio.com) should you require accommodations at any point during our virtual interview processes.

Description & Requirements
who we are
lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. Setting the bar in technical fabrics and functional design, we create transformational products and experiences that support people in moving, growing, connecting, and being well. We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.
about this team
The MP&A Product Management team is focused on improving processes and systems that impact lululemon’s merchandising, planning, and allocations teams. We identify key business requirements that support our global MP&A processes ultimately helping lululemon live into our global growth strategies. We provide the business process context necessary to guide technical decision making, while leveraging our connection with the business to enroll stakeholders on key process changes and impacts.
core responsibilities
The Manager, Product Management will be responsible for discovering, defining, & delivering, products that support the MP&A business teams. They will work in close collaboration with key stakeholders from the business and their IT partners to strategize and execute against the strategic goals for lululemon. This means they lead cross-functional teams from a product's conception all the way through to its launch and improvement.
Core Accountabilities:
Strategy
Responsible for the creation of the 6 month – 1 year product strategy including developing tactical & strategic roadmaps
Prioritizes the roadmap against business objectives and OKRs
Internally recognized as a go-to-person for complex technical and business matters.
Complexity & Delivery
Leads the strategic direction for PI planning
Responsible for the overall execution of the Delivery Plan
Anticipates implementation challenges and develops mitigation strategies to minimize risk
Works on large, complex activities that cross domains/functional groups
Collaboration & Communication
Ability to communicate roadmaps and progress against the roadmap to key stakeholders & IT partners
Lead & develop team members to effectively gather requirements and deliver solutions that meet the business needs
Manage 3rd party relationships / vendors
Proactively solves potential problems with other functions to avoid unnecessary conflict
Contributes actively to build common ground for cooperation
qualifications
Bachelor's degree in business, computer science, information technology or a related field
5+ years work experience in retail or supply chain functions
5+ years work experience in product management
Excellent spoken and written communication skills (verbal and non-verbal)
Ability to lead and influence teams
Proficient with Microsoft Office and system mapping tools like Visio
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Ability to manage and complete multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment
must haves
Acknowledge the presence of choice in every moment and take personal responsibility for your life.
Possess an entrepreneurial spirit and continuously innovate to achieve great results.
Communicate with honesty and kindness and create the space for others to do the same.
Lead with courage, knowing the possibility of greatness is bigger than the fear of failure.
Foster connection by putting people first and building trusting relationships.
Integrate fun and joy as a way of being and working, aka doesn’t take yourself too seriously.
additional notes
Authorization to work in Canada is required for this role.
compensation and benefits package
lululemon’s compensation offerings are grounded in a pay-for-performance philosophy that recognizes exceptional individual and team performance. The typical hiring range for this position is from $141,800 - $186,100 CAD annually ; the base pay offered is based on market location and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and internal equity. As part of our total rewards offering, permanent employees in this position may be eligible for our competitive annual bonus program, subject to program eligibility requirements.
At lululemon, investing in our people is a top priority. We believe that when life works, work works. We strive to be the place where inclusive leaders come to develop and enable all to be well. Recognizing our teams for their performance and dedication, other components of our total rewards offerings include support of career development, wellbeing, and personal growth:
Extended health and dental benefits, and mental health plans
Paid time off
Savings and retirement plan matching
Generous employee discount
Fitness & yoga classes
Parenthood top-up
Extensive catalog of development course offerings
People networks, mentorship programs, and leadership series (to name a few)
Note: The incentive programs, benefits, and perks have certain eligibility requirements. The Company reserves the right to alter these incentive programs, benefits, and perks in whole or in part at any time without advance notice.
workplace arrangement
In-person collaboration and connection is important to our culture. Work is performed onsite, minimum 4 days per week.

Description & Requirements
Who We Are
lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. Setting the bar in technical fabrics and functional design, we create transformational products and experiences that support people in moving, growing, connecting, and being well. We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.
Job Summary
The Product Operations Lead is a part of the store leadership team responsible for executing on the store product strategy, including product operations and inventory management. They are responsible for leading inventory shifts, overseeing all back of house (BOH) product operations, and ensuring both the floor and BOH are stocked and well-organized. The Product Operations Lead provides input to team member performance evaluations, recommendations into store hiring decisions, and acts as Supervisor on Duty (SOD) while leading inventory shifts. The Product Operations Lead also oversees and delivers a world-class guest (i.e., customer) experience when scheduled to work on the floor.
Core Responsibilities of the Job
Collaborate with store leadership to bring product strategy to life.
Proactively plan, prioritize, manage, and lead inventory processing and accuracy activities in accordance with standard operating procedures (SOPs).
Ensure execution of product actions (e.g., pull backs, consolidations, repricing).
Engage team members in inventory management by creating a fun and productive atmosphere for the shift.
Monitor product levels and communicate findings to support sell-through strategy and optimal product availability for the guest.
Review and interpret daily business data and metrics to inform actions, for example analyzing product sell-through data to provide recommendations to store leadership regarding product focus or, for outlets, pricing.
Participate in the store’s hiring process, including recruitment, selection and hiring recommendations, onboarding, and training.
Address team member performance and support their ongoing learning and development by providing direct feedback and in-the-moment recognition, coaching, demonstrations, and hands-on experiences.
Contribute to a respectful and inclusive team environment by establishing supportive working relationships with team members.
When serving as Supervisor on Duty during store open hours, move dynamically and lead from the floor to ensure every guest receives technical product education and establish a world-class guest experience.
Job Requirements
Eligibility
Must be legally authorized to work in the country in which the store is located
Must have the ability to travel to assigned store with reliable transportation methods
Schedule/Availability
The work schedule can vary based on store needs
Shifts are typically scheduled: mornings, afternoons, evenings, weekends, and holidays
In addition, during peak timeframes, special events, or other circumstances, the schedule may include early mornings or late nights/overnights for some team members
Experience
1 year of work experience
Some experience with inventory management, product or visual merchandising, stocking, or planning and logistics including using business technology to accomplish work
Some experience in leading, mentoring, delegating or process implementation with others
Job Assets (i.e., nice to have; not required)
Education: High school diploma/GED/equivalent, or above
Experience (not necessarily the only focus of a role): retail, sales, distribution center, or warehouse operations related; reviewing and interpreting business reports and metrics to inform action
For Experiential stores with food/beverage service only : Food safety and/or liquor service certification
What We Look For
Inclusion & Diversity: Creates/supports an inclusive environment that values/celebrates differences
Integrity: Behaves in an honest, fair, and ethical manner
Adaptability/Agility: Navigates uncertainty and ambiguity and can change priorities in a fast-paced environment; recovers quickly from setbacks
Leadership: Is able and desires to lead and inspire others; motivates, empowers, develops, and directs people as they work
Collaboration and Teamwork: Works productively with and supports others to achieve common goals; seeks connections, partnerships, and diverse perspectives
Decision Making/Problem Solving: Identifies opportunities for improvement; evaluates alternatives and makes effective, timely decisions
Planning and Organizing: Plans and organizes work in a clear and efficient manner to ensure completion in alignment with priorities
Interactive Communication: Conveys information effectively and understands information shared while interacting with others
Work Context (e.g., environment, interactions, physical)
Work involves moving through the store, sometimes in the front of the house with bright lights and loud music, and sometimes in the back of the house with no windows or natural light
Work is accomplished as part of a team, sometimes independently, and sometimes using a computer or other technical devices
Work may occasionally involve moving boxes weighing up to 30 lbs (13.6 kg) or using ladders to reach materials
For Experiential stores with food/beverage service only: Work may involve using industrial kitchen equipment and exposure to heat in order to prepare food or beverages
Compensation & Benefits Package
Base Pay Range : $24.25 - $28.00/hour, subject to minimum wage in the location
Target Bonus: $2.00/hour
Total Target Base Pay Range : $26.25 - $30.00/hour

The base pay offered is based on market location and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and internal equity. As part of our offerings, employees in this position may be eligible for our competitive bonus program and equity offerings, subject to program eligibility requirements.

Extended health and dental benefits, and mental health plans
Paid time off

Qui nous sommes
lululemon est une entreprise innovante de vêtements performants pour le yoga, la course à pied, l’entraînement et d’autres activités sportives. En établissant des standards élevés en matière de tissus techniques et de design fonctionnel, nous créons des produits et des expériences qui aident les gens à bouger, à croître, à tisser des liens et à se sentir bien. Nous devons notre succès à nos produits innovants, à l’importance que nous accordons à nos magasins, à notre engagement envers notre personnel et aux connexions incroyables que nous établissons dans chaque communauté où nous nous trouvons. En tant qu’entreprise, nous nous efforçons de créer un changement positif pour construire un avenir sain et prospère. Cela consiste notamment à créer un environnement équitable, inclusif et axé sur la croissance pour notre personnel.
Résumé du poste
Le ou la responsable des activités-produits fait partie de l’équipe de gestion du magasin qui est responsable de l’exécution de la stratégie générale des produits, notamment les activités-produits et la gestion des stocks. Il ou elle est responsable de diriger les quarts de travail consacrés à l’inventaire, de superviser toutes les activités-produits liées à l’arrière-boutique et de veiller à ce que le plancher et l’arrière-boutique soient bien remplis et bien ordonnés. Le ou la responsable des activités-produits fournit des perspectives en matière d’évaluations du rendement des membres d’équipe, des recommandations en lien avec les décisions d’embauche du magasin et agit à titre de superviseur(e) en service tout en gérant les quarts de travail consacrés aux inventaires. Également, le ou la responsable des activités-produits supervise et offre une expérience-invité (c.-à-d. expérience-client) de classe mondiale quand il ou elle doit travailler sur le plancher.
Principales responsabilités liées au poste
Collabore avec l’équipe de gestion du magasin pour donner vie à la stratégie liée aux produits.
De façon proactive, planifie, priorise, gère et dirige les activités de traitement et d’exactitude des stocks conformément aux méthodes d’exploitation standards (MES).
Assure l’exécution des mesures liées aux produits (p. ex. les retraits, les consolidations, la révision des prix, etc.).
Motive les membres d’équipe en matière de gestion de stocks en créant une atmosphère amusante et productive tout au long du quart.
Surveille les niveaux de produits et communique ses observations pour soutenir la stratégie d’écoulement des stocks et l’optimisation de la disponibilité des produits pour les invités.
Consulte et interprète des données et les indicateurs commerciaux quotidiens pour orienter des mesures, comme en analysant les données d’écoulement des produits afin de donner des recommandations à l’équipe de gestion du magasin relativement aux produits à prioriser ou, dans le cas des entrepôts, à l’établissement des prix.
Participe au processus d’embauche du magasin, notamment au recrutement, à la sélection, aux recommandations liées à l’embauche, à l’orientation et l’intégration, et à la formation.
Gère le rendement des membres d’équipe et soutient leur apprentissage et leur développement continus en leur offrant une rétroaction directe, de la reconnaissance immédiate, de l’accompagnement professionnel, des démonstrations et des expériences pratiques en temps opportun.
Favorise un environnement d’équipe à la fois respectueux et inclusif en établissant des relations d’aide au travail avec les membres de l’équipe.
À titre de superviseur(e) en service pendant l’ouverture du magasin, se déplace avec dynamisme et gère le plancher afin que tous les invités reçoivent de l’éducation technique sur les produits et de créer une expérience-invité de classe mondiale.
Exigences du poste
Admissibilité
Doit être légalement autorisé(e) à travailler dans le pays dans lequel le magasin est situé.
Doit avoir la capacité de se rendre au magasin assigné en utilisant des moyens de transport fiables.
Horaire et disponibilité
L’horaire de travail peut varier en fonction des besoins du magasin.
Les quarts de travail ont normalement lieu les matins, les après-midi, les soirs, les fins de semaine et les jours fériés.
De plus, pendant les périodes achalandées, les événements spéciaux ou d’autres circonstances, l’horaire de certains membres d’équipe peut inclure des petits matins ou des soirées tardives/des nuits complètes.
Expérience
Un an d’expérience professionnelle.
De l’expérience en matière de gestion des stocks, de marchandisage de produits ou visuel, de réapprovisionnement ou de planification, et en logistique, y compris l’utilisation de technologie commerciale pour accomplir des tâches.
De l’expérience en gestion, en accompagnement professionnel, en délégation ou en mise en œuvre de processus avec d’autres.
Atouts pour l’emploi (c.-à-d. souhaitable, mais pas obligatoire).
Éducation : diplôme d’études secondaires, formation générale, ou équivalent ou éducation supérieure.
Expérience (pas nécessairement liée à la responsabilité essentielle d’un rôle) : vente au détail, vente, centre de distribution ou expérience liée à des activités d’entrepôt; consultation et interprétation de rapports et d’indicateurs commerciaux pour orienter des mesures.
Magasins expérientiels servant des aliments ou de la boisson seulement : certification en salubrité alimentaire ou en service de spiritueux.
Nos besoins
Inclusion et diversité : crée/soutient un environnement inclusif qui valorise/célèbre les différences.
Intégrité : se comporte de manière honnête, équitable et éthique.
Adaptabilité/agilité : sait gérer l’incertitude et l’ambiguïté et peut changer de priorités dans un environnement en évolution rapide; se remet rapidement des échecs.
Leadership : a la capacité et le désir de diriger et d’inspirer les autres; motive, responsabilise, développe et dirige les personnes dans leur travail.
Collaboration et travail d’équipe : travaille de manière productive avec les autres et les soutient pour atteindre des objectifs communs; recherche la création de liens, des partenariats et des points de vue divers.
Prise de décisions/résolution de problèmes : repère les occasions d’amélioration; évalue les solutions de rechange et prend des décisions judicieuses en temps opportun.
Planification et organisation : planifie et organise le travail d’une façon claire et efficace pour garantir qu’il soit terminé conformément aux priorités.

Job Summary
The Product Operations Lead is a part of the store leadership team responsible for executing on the store product strategy, including product operations and inventory management. They are responsible for leading inventory shifts, overseeing all back of house (BOH) product operations, and ensuring both the floor and BOH are stocked and well-organized. The Product Operations Lead provides input to team member performance evaluations, recommendations into store hiring decisions, and acts as Supervisor on Duty (SOD) while leading inventory shifts. The Product Operations Lead also oversees and delivers a world-class guest (i.e., customer) experience when scheduled to work on the floor.
Core Responsibilities of the Job
Collaborate with store leadership to bring product strategy to life.
Proactively plan, prioritize, manage, and lead inventory processing and accuracy activities in accordance with standard operating procedures (SOPs).
Ensure execution of product actions (e.g., pull backs, consolidations, repricing).
Engage team members in inventory management by creating a fun and productive atmosphere for the shift.
Monitor product levels and communicate findings to support sell-through strategy and optimal product availability for the guest.
Review and interpret daily business data and metrics to inform actions, for example analyzing product sell-through data to provide recommendations to store leadership regarding product focus or, for outlets, pricing.
Participate in the store’s hiring process, including recruitment, selection and hiring recommendations, onboarding, and training.
Address team member performance and support their ongoing learning and development by providing direct feedback and in-the-moment recognition, coaching, demonstrations, and hands-on experiences.
Contribute to a respectful and inclusive team environment by establishing supportive working relationships with team members.
When serving as Supervisor on Duty during store open hours, move dynamically and lead from the floor to ensure every guest receives technical product education and establish a world-class guest experience.

Must have the ability to travel to assigned store with reliable transportation methods

In addition, during peak timeframes, special events, or other circumstances, the schedule may include early mornings or late nights/overnights for some team members
Experience
1 year of work experience
Some experience with inventory management, product or visual merchandising, stocking, or planning and logistics including using business technology to accomplish work
Some experience in leading, mentoring, delegating or process implementation with others

Education: High school diploma/GED/equivalent, or above
Experience (not necessarily the only focus of a role): retail, sales, distribution center, or warehouse operations related; reviewing and interpreting business reports and metrics to inform action
